items.title: Composite midpoint rule on a uniform grid
items.statement: For a<b, integer n>=1, and f:[a,b]->R, return h times the sum of f at the n panel midpoints, where h=(b-a)/n.
items.strategy: A finite exact-real weighted sum; invalid intervals or panel counts return an explicit status.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Composite Simpson rule on an even uniform grid
items.statement: For a<b and even integer n>=2, return h/3 times the sum over n/2 two-panel blocks of the two endpoints plus four times the midpoint; expansion gives weights 1,4,2,...,4,1.
items.strategy: A finite exact-real weighted sum over n/2 two-panel blocks.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Midpoint panel error kernel and second-derivative bound
items.statement: For f in C^2[a,b], the panel midpoint error equals the integral of a nonnegative piecewise-quadratic kernel times f'' and is bounded by (b-a)^3 max|f''|/24.
items.strategy: Apply integration by parts twice on the two half-panels, then use kernel positivity and its exact integral.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Composite midpoint error bound for a twice continuously differentiable function
items.statement: For f in C^2[a,b], n>=1 and h=(b-a)/n, the composite midpoint error is at most (b-a)h^2 max|f''|/24.
items.strategy: Apply the local midpoint kernel estimate to every panel, use additivity, and sum the panel bounds.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, Theorem 7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Peano kernel identity for one Simpson panel
items.statement: On a panel [a,b] of width L, the Simpson error is the integral of K_{a,b} f^(4), where K is the scaled piecewise quartic kernel; it is nonpositive and has integral of its absolute value L^5/2880.
items.strategy: Integrate by parts four times on each half, compute the jump contribution at the midpoint, and integrate the kernel.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Composite Simpson rule is exact through cubic degree
items.statement: For every p(x)=c0+c1*x+c2*x^2+c3*x^3 and every even n>=2, composite Simpson integrates p exactly on [a,b].
items.strategy: The Peano kernel identity has zero remainder when the fourth derivative vanishes; sum over the two-panel blocks.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Composite Simpson error bound for a four-times continuously differentiable function
items.statement: For f in C^4[a,b], even n>=2 and h=(b-a)/n, the composite Simpson error is at most (b-a)h^4 max|f^(4)|/180.
items.strategy: Scale the one-panel Peano kernel to every two-panel block, add the block errors, and use the triangle inequality.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Convex data bracket the integral between composite midpoint and trapezoid values
items.statement: For convex f in C^2[a,b], the composite midpoint value is no larger than the integral, which is no larger than the published composite trapezoid value.
items.strategy: Use the midpoint error kernel for the lower bound and integrate each convex endpoint chord for the upper bound.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.1
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Simpson rule integrates a quadratic exactly on one two-panel block
items.statement: For f(x)=x^2 on [0,2] and n=2, both the exact integral and composite Simpson value are 8/3.
items.strategy: Evaluate the antiderivative and the three Simpson node values.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6

items.title: Simpson rule integrates a cubic exactly on one two-panel block
items.statement: For f(x)=x^3 on [0,2] and n=2, both the exact integral and composite Simpson value are 4.
items.strategy: Evaluate the antiderivative and the three Simpson node values.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 7, §7.2
Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Fundamentals of Numerical Computation, §5.6
